title: Calixtus: man can resist grace, yet can care for the means of salvation
source_text: VII. Ex ejus enim sententia, nullum dubium est, quin homo oblatam gratiam spernere, rejicere, & Spiritui Sancto fidem operaturo resistere possit. Quoniam Deus homines absoluta sua potentia non trahit & convertit, verum hoc facit secundum ordinem & modum quem semel instituit. Contra vero certum est, hominem posse solicitum esse de sua salute, posse curam suscipere de mediis ad eam, juxta illud, Multi quaerent intrare & non poterunt. Quippe posse hominem audire verbum Dei, imo cum omni alacritate verbum suscipere & scrutari studio discendae & cognoscendae veritatis.
pass_a_gloss: VII. For in his opinion, there is no doubt, but that man can spurn, reject the grace offered, & resist the Holy Spirit when about to work faith. Because God does not draw & convert men by his absolute power, but does this according to the order & manner which he once instituted. On the other hand it is certain, that man can be solicitous of his salvation, can take care about the means to it, according to that saying, Many will seek to enter & will not be able. For man can hear the word of God, indeed with all eagerness receive the word & search it with zeal for learning & knowing the truth.
pass_b_english: Thesis VII. On his view there is no doubt that a person can scorn and reject the grace offered and resist the Holy Spirit when he is about to produce faith, since God does not draw and convert people by his absolute power but according to the order and pattern he laid down once for all.

On the other hand, he holds, it is certain that a person can be anxious for his salvation and can take trouble over the means to it, as in the saying, 'Many will seek to enter and will not be able.' A person can hear God's word, and even receive it with all readiness and study it in an effort to learn and come to know the truth.
